blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Campbell Valley
The ground in Campbell Valley

items.t: Fee-simple acreage parcels: a Campbell Valley parcel is fee-simple unless title shows otherwise — no strata, no Form B, no strata fees on the parcel itself; Township zoning, ALR status (where applicable) and registered charges govern.

blocks.text: Good to know about Campbell Valley

items.t: The park is regional, and horses are in its mandate: Campbell Valley Regional Park is a Metro Vancouver regional park whose trail network serves horseback riders alongside walkers and cyclists — the infrastructure behind the sub-area's equestrian framing.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley Acreages and Farms: streets and boundaries

items.t: Campbell Valley is the rural valley in south Langley Township around 200 Street and 16 Avenue, and its centrepiece is parkland, not a subdivision.
The Little Campbell River runs through the park, and the Little River Loop trail crosses it twice on raised boardwalks.
The Township's GeoSource tool is where a buyer checks a Campbell Valley parcel's zoning, plan area and watercourses lot by lot.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley Acreages and Farms: the housing stock

items.t: Park land is not housing stock: the Annand/Rowlatt Farmstead (buildings from 1898) and the Lochiel Schoolhouse (built 1924, moved to the park in 1988) sit inside Campbell Valley Regional Park as heritage sites.
Equestrian use shapes the parcels: Metro Vancouver lists equestrian facilities, a riding ring and horse unloading in the park, and nearly 17 kilometres (km) of horse trails.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley Acreages and Farms: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Where a parcel is in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR), the Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) caps a principal residence at 500 square metres (m²) total floor area, with no more than 1,000 m² of fill for its construction.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley Acreages and Farms: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Dogs must be on leash throughout Campbell Valley Regional Park except in the leash-optional area next to 4 Avenue, which affects acreages that back onto the park.
Cycling is allowed only on the Perimeter Trail in the park, and cycling is not permitted on the Shaggy Mane Trail at all.
McLean Pond is closed to fishing by provincial regulation dating to April 1, 2017, to protect native animals.
School catchment is address-based: School District 35 (Langley) says its School Locator Tool determines the catchment school from a street address or housing development name.
Park hours change with the season — Metro Vancouver lists 7:00 am–6:00 pm from November 3 to December 31 — so evening trail traffic beside nearby parcels is seasonal.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley Acreages and Farms: costs and taxes

items.t: The Township tax notice bundles general Township taxes plus levies for roads, drainage, solid waste and capital projects, and taxes collected for other authorities — drainage and solid waste matter on acreages.
The Speculation and Vacancy Tax (SVT) taxable-area list includes the Township of Langley, so a residential parcel owner there must check the declaration duty on the Province's page.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley Acreages and Farms: getting around

items.t: Transit reaches the park, not most acreages: Metro Vancouver states a regular bus stop is near the park entrance at 200th Street and 20th Avenue, Langley.
TransLink route 566 serves the South Valley entrance on weekends and holidays from June 8 to September 6, 2026, as Metro Vancouver states.
Cyclists can connect from the park to the South Langley Regional Trail at its south-east corner, and to the Fernridge Trail and High Point multi-use trail nearby.

blocks.text: Campbell Valley Acreages and Farms: risks and due diligence

items.t: Flood and watercourse checks start in GeoSource: the Township directs buyers to activate the Environment layer to view watercourses and classifications for a parcel.
The Little Campbell River is a working watercourse through the valley — the park's Little River Loop crosses it twice — so riparian setbacks on a bordering parcel need a lot-specific check.
In the ALR, building can trigger a Notice of Intent for fill, health authority approval for septic, and floodplain or riparian approvals, as the ALC lists.

faq.q: Can I convert a Campbell Valley acreage to bare-land strata?
faq.a: No strata conversion is verified for any parcel here, and on ALR ground depositing a strata plan IS a subdivision and needs ALC permission (Bulletin 09 s.6).

faq.q: What were Campbell Valley's own market figures in September 2026?
faq.a: The Langley community medians are board context, expressly not Campbell Valley's.

faq.q: When are Township of Langley property taxes due?
faq.a: Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty at midnight July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% at midnight September 3, 2026.

faq.q: Can I build a second full house on a Campbell Valley acreage?
faq.a: Not as of right on most parcels. In the ALR the ALC allows one principal residence, plus one additional detached residence only if conditions are met — up to 90 m² on properties 40 hectares (ha) or less — and Township zoning may be stricter, so confirm both layers for the specific lot before you buy.

faq.q: Why do so many listings mention horses?
faq.a: Because the park next door is built for them. Metro Vancouver lists nearly 17 km of equestrian trails, the 11 km Shaggy Mane Trail shared with pedestrians, horse-trailer parking at Campbell Downs Equestrian Centre, and a riding ring — so trailer access and fencing on the parcel itself are practical checks, not extras.

faq.q: Does small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) give me 3–4 units here?
faq.a: Usually no on a large rural lot. The Township states lots larger than 4,050 m² (1 acre) are not eligible for SSMUH, and eligible lots must be inside the Urban Containment Boundary and connected to both municipal water and sewer; other lots get one unit plus one suite or accessory dwelling unit (ADU), depending on zoning.
